supersedes: Initial REVIEW.json/TXT preserved by parent under first-attempt. The initial review missed the concrete reserved-test POSIX exclusion defect described below.

resolved_review_findings.title: POSIX branch incorrectly expected intentionally excluded reserved-name fixtures in captured output
resolved_review_findings.discovery: Parent found this after the initial independent review; independent reproduction confirmed exactly two failures in the complete 20-case POSIX branch model.
resolved_review_findings.cause: The __pycache__/NUL and NUL.tmp host cases omitted their generic exclusion expectations. Windows rejected these fixtures as intended, masking the wrong POSIX expected inventory.
resolved_review_findings.impact: The required reserved-payload job would fail those two checks on POSIX despite correct production collector behavior. This is a test portability failure, not an addon/runtime or production collector failure.
resolved_review_findings.repair: Both host cases now declare their existing generic exclusions. The existing modeled_posix_reserved_names_preserved case additionally includes both excluded fixtures and checks their omission.
resolved_review_findings.windows_strength_preserved: unsafe=True, alias settings, fixture creation, should_reject condition and rejection assertion remain intact. The excluded list is used only in the non-rejection branch. Two isolated Windows mutations each fail the intended single exclusion-order control.

review_correction_note: The first review did not exercise the entire test under its POSIX branch and missed two incorrect expected inventories. This follow-up reproduces that failure before correction, checks all twenty cases afterward, and proves retention of both Windows early-rejection controls with independent mutations.
